newsitem.title: USA: US senator threatens to stall Pena confirmation.
newsitem.headline: US senator threatens to stall Pena confirmation.

text.p: U.S. Sen. Rod Grams said Thursday he would block a full Senate vote on confirming Federico Pena to be energy secretary until he gets answers on how the Clinton administration plans to dispose of radioactive waste from nuclear power plants.

In remarks on the Senate floor, the Minnesota Republican said he would object to efforts to bring up Pena's nomination "at this time," and said he was "willing to work with my colleagues in ensuring that a final vote is not taken before a specific constructive respose is given" from the administration.

"While I hold out hope that we will receive such an answer from Mr. Pena in the immediate future, accordingly I would object to any unanimous consent agreement to bring up Mr. Pena's nomination for a vote at this time," Grams said.
Grams has complained that the administration has not offered a plan to store or take possession of nuclear waste accumulating at reactors around the country.

Under a 1982 law, the federal government assumes responsibility for the waste next year, and utilities have paid some $12 billion into a federal fund to set up a central waste dump. However, that has not been built.
The Energy Department had no immediate comment on Grams' statement.
